agent_reason: Both are US healthcare providers serving patients referred by clinicians and paid mainly by insurers and government payers. The offerings differ. Accendra delivers home respiratory, sleep and durable medical equipment plus chronic-condition supplies to patients at home. U.S. Physical Therapy runs outpatient physical and occupational therapy clinics, plus industrial injury prevention and practice management. The customers (patients and payers) overlap but the products do not.
notes_barbara:
Different products and functional buyers

USPH owns and operates outpatient physical and occupational therapy clinics treating patients with musculoskeletal injuries, post-surgical needs and work-related injuries. ACH focuses on home respiratory and sleep equipment and chronic-care supplies.

agent_reason: Accendra delivers home medical equipment (oxygen, CPAP, DME) and chronic-care supplies to patients at home. Ensign owns and operates skilled nursing and assisted living facilities. The products differ and so does the operating model, which is delivery and supplies versus running residential care facilities. Both are paid by Medicare, Medicaid and private insurers for senior and post-acute patients, but that overlap is only in the payer and the broad healthcare sector.
notes_barbara:
Partial operating overlap. Different business mix

ENSG owns and operates skilled nursing facilities, senior living communities and related healthcare businesses. ACH focuses on home respiratory and sleep equipment and chronic-care supplies.

agent_reason: Accendra delivers home respiratory, sleep, diabetes, wound care, urology and ostomy equipment and supplies to patients at home. UHS owns and operates acute care hospitals, behavioral health facilities and emergency and outpatient centers. The offerings differ: home equipment and supplies against facility-based care. Both serve patients and are paid largely by insurers and government programs, so customers and reimbursement overlap. That is overlap on customers only, not on product, which makes them adjacent.
notes_barbara:
Different products and functional buyers

UHS owns and operates acute care hospitals, behavioral health facilities, and ambulatory centers. ACH focuses on home respiratory and sleep equipment and chronic-care supplies.

agent_reason: Both are insurance underwriters earning premiums and investment income, with high state insurance regulation. But AFG sells commercial specialty P&C to businesses via brokers. Security National sells life/pre-need insurance, title insurance and mortgages, mostly to consumers and real estate and funeral channels, and owns funeral homes. The overlap is only the general insurance model.
notes_barbara:
Different end markets and offerings

SNFC.A operates three segments: life insurance and pre-need funeral products, title insurance and escrow settlement services, and residential mortgage origination. AFG focuses on commercial specialty P&C underwriting.

agent_reason: Both are risk-bearing specialty commercial P&C insurers. They sell to businesses in niche industries such as transportation and nonprofit, and the sites describe decentralized specialty units. Both earn premiums plus investment income. Old Republic also has a title insurance line, but its specialty commercial insurance covers the target's whole business.
notes_barbara:
Commercial underwriting overlap. Different portfolio mix

Old Republic overlaps AFG in commercial casualty, auto and property insurance. Its separate title insurance business adds exposure to real estate transactions.

agent_reason: AFG is a risk-bearing specialty P&C insurer. It underwrites policies and earns premiums plus investment income. Brown & Brown is an insurance intermediary. It places coverage for clients and earns commissions and fees without carrying underwriting risk. Both serve commercial insurance buyers, but they make money in different ways. Brown & Brown also sells to individuals and handles employee benefits. In the value chain, Brown & Brown is a distribution channel for carriers like AFG.
notes_barbara:
Commercial policyholder overlap. Different risk model

Brown & Brown places commercial insurance and earns brokerage and program fees. AFG underwrites policies and earns premiums while bearing insurance risk.

agent_reason: AFG is a specialty P&C insurance carrier that underwrites commercial risk and earns premiums plus investment income. Baldwin is an insurance distributor and advisor that earns commissions and fees. It places coverage with carriers for businesses and individuals, and it also sells personal insurance, benefits and wealth management. The two sit in the same industry but along different parts of the value chain. Baldwin is closer to a distribution channel for carriers like AFG than to a competitor.
notes_barbara:
Commercial policyholder overlap. Different risk model

Baldwin places coverage and manages programs for businesses. AFG earns premiums and assumes underwriting risk as a specialty carrier.

agent_reason: Both are P&C insurance carriers earning premiums plus investment income and selling through independent agents and brokers. AFG writes specialty commercial lines nationally for businesses. Kingstone mainly writes personal lines, mostly homeowners, in the Northeast. The only product overlap is a small commercial auto line at Kingstone. The customers are mostly different, so this is adjacent.
notes_barbara:
Different core policyholders. Limited vehicle coverage overlap

Kingstone primarily writes personal property coverage and has a niche for-hire vehicle offering. AFG focuses on specialty commercial risks.

agent_reason: Both are commercial-stage branded prescription biopharma companies. Akebia focuses on kidney disease drugs. BioMarin focuses on rare genetic diseases, such as achondroplasia, hemophilia A and lysosomal storage diseases. The therapeutic areas and treating specialists differ, with nephrology and dialysis providers on one side and rare-disease centers on the other. The overlap is the business model and generic channels, such as specialty pharmacies and wholesalers. Both also earn licensing or royalty revenue.
notes_barbara:
Different indications and prescribers

BioMarin focuses on rare genetic diseases, while Akebia serves renal disease patients and prescribers. Specialty drug commercialization alone provides limited overlap.

agent_reason: Both are commercial-stage, single-specialty biopharma companies that sell prescription drugs and have a similar business model. Akebia sells renal drugs (kidney disease, dialysis). Ironwood sells gastrointestinal drugs. The therapeutic areas and the prescribers differ (nephrology and dialysis providers versus gastroenterology). Overlap is limited to the industry and business model, so this is adjacent rather than direct.
notes_barbara:
Different products and functional buyers

IRWD develops and commercializes prescription medicines for gastrointestinal diseases. AKBA focuses on kidney disease medicines distributed through renal care channels.

agent_reason: Both are commercial-stage branded prescription drug companies with FDA-approved products, but they treat different diseases. Akebia focuses on kidney disease and Indivior on opioid use disorder. The channels overlap (wholesalers and pharmacies), but the prescribers and patients differ (nephrology versus addiction treatment). This is adjacent, not a direct competitor.
notes_barbara:
Different products and functional buyers

INDV develops and sells prescription medicines for opioid use disorder and related addiction and mental health conditions. AKBA focuses on kidney disease medicines distributed through renal care channels.

agent_reason: AMETEK designs and manufactures its own instruments, sensors and electromechanical components. DSG is a specialty distributor that resells other makers' products. Its main lines are MRO supplies, fasteners and C-parts, plus supply chain services. Only the TestEquity unit touches test and measurement, and it resells that equipment rather than making it. The two earn money differently and sit at different points in the value chain.
notes_barbara:
Partial operating overlap. Different business mix

DSGR distributes maintenance, repair and operations (MRO) products, fasteners and other industrial supplies to industrial, commercial and vehicle-aftermarket customers. AME focuses on engineered instruments and electromechanical products.

agent_reason: Both are diversified makers of niche, highly engineered instruments and components. They overlap in test and measurement and diagnostic equipment, aerospace and defense components, and power and utility markets. Both sell to B2B and defense customers, mainly through direct sales plus distributors, and both add calibration and aftermarket services. ESCO is a narrower version of AMETEK's portfolio, but the product and customer overlap is substantial in several segments.
notes_barbara:
Partial operating overlap. Different business mix

ESE designs and manufactures highly engineered products for aerospace and defense, utility power delivery, and industrial and test markets. AME focuses on engineered instruments and electromechanical products.

agent_reason: Both run accredited, online-first education businesses with some career-oriented programs. APEI serves adult and postsecondary learners (military, veterans, nursing students) and earns tuition. Stride's cited offerings are K-12 online public and private schools, tutoring, and a talent platform for families and students. The overlap is in the online delivery model and the education industry. The core customers differ, so this is adjacent, not direct.
notes_barbara:
Different core offering and revenue model

LRN provides online and blended K-12 education: curriculum, technology and school operations for virtual public schools, plus career learning programs. APEI focuses on online and campus-based postsecondary education for adults and healthcare students.

agent_reason: APi is a branch-based service and installation contractor. It does inspection, maintenance and installation of fire protection, life safety, HVAC, elevator and security systems. SPX is a manufacturer of engineered HVAC products and detection and measurement equipment, sold through distributors and reps. The only overlap is HVAC, and there SPX is an equipment supplier, not an installer or servicer. The two share some building-owner and contractor customers, but SPX has no fire, life-safety, elevator or security services. Its other main segment, detection and measurement (locators, fare collection, navigation lights), has no match at APi. Revenue models differ: product sales versus service contracts and installation projects.
notes_barbara:
Partial operating overlap. Different business mix

SPXC designs and manufactures heating, ventilation and cooling products, plus detection and measurement systems such as underground utility locators, bus fare collection, communication technologies and obstruction lighting. APG focuses on field installation, inspection and maintenance of building and infrastructure systems.

agent_reason: APi Group is a services provider (safety and specialty services such as inspection, maintenance and installation) that earns money from service fees and contracts. Ferguson is a wholesale distributor that resells plumbing, HVAC, waterworks and fire products to contractors through branches and distribution centers. Fire protection and HVAC overlap only loosely. Ferguson's contractor customers are more likely suppliers or customers of APi than direct competitors.
notes_barbara:
Partial operating overlap. Different business mix

FERG distributes plumbing, heating, ventilation and air conditioning products, waterworks, fire protection and industrial piping products. APG focuses on field installation, inspection and maintenance of building and infrastructure systems.

agent_reason: AZZ sells galvanizing and coil coating as a service on customer-owned steel, plus coated coil. Perma-Pipe manufactures engineered pre-insulated piping, containment and leak detection systems for specific projects. Its anti-corrosion coating is applied to its own pipe and is not sold as a stand-alone coating service. End markets overlap only loosely (infrastructure and industrial). Buyers differ: AZZ sells to fabricators and coil users, Perma-Pipe to district energy, mechanical and pipeline contractors.
notes_barbara:
Partial corrosion-protection overlap. Different core offering

Perma-Pipe offers coating and finishing within engineered piping systems. AZZ provides galvanizing and coil coating across broader fabricated steel markets.

agent_reason: Target provides concrete pumping and concrete washout waste services to construction contractors. The comp provides fire protection, security, elevator, HVAC and specialty infrastructure inspection, maintenance and installation services to building owners. The offerings do not overlap. Customers overlap only loosely, at the level of commercial and industrial construction and facilities. Both are branch-based service businesses, but that is too generic to count.
notes_barbara:
Construction services overlap. Different core work

APi’s specialty operations include infrastructure and concrete work. Concrete Pumping Holdings focuses on concrete placement and washout, while APi has a broader mix led by life safety services.

agent_reason: Target is a service and rental operator that places concrete with its own pump fleet and operators, and also runs concrete waste removal. Comp manufactures and sells water, wastewater, fire and industrial pumps through distributors. The only link is the word pump, plus a small construction customer overlap.
notes_barbara:
Construction contractor overlap. Different product and revenue models

Gorman-Rupp sells jobsite dewatering pumps. Concrete Pumping Holdings earns service revenue from operated concrete placement and washout.

agent_reason: Both operate casual full-service restaurants for consumer diners, and both serve beer and drinks. The target also runs a separate package liquor retail business (Big Daddy's), which the comp doesn't have. Under the multi-business rule, a comp that matches only one material business gets at most 1. The comp is also a national steakhouse brand with international licensing. The target is a regional South Florida seafood bar and grill.
notes_barbara:
Core product and customer overlap

TXRH operates full-service casual dining restaurants serving hand-cut steaks, ribs, chicken and made-from-scratch sides to dine-in and takeout guests. BDL focuses on casual seafood restaurants and package liquor stores.

agent_reason: Both are vertically integrated, acquisitive Southeast civil infrastructure contractors. They self-perform paving and site work with their own crews and equipment, and they overlap in NC, SC and GA. They are paid per project. The comp adds asphalt and aggregate production, and the target adds utilities and drilling and blasting. Neither difference changes the core overlap.
notes_barbara:
Paving overlap. Different project mix

Construction Partners serves road and paving projects and operates asphalt plants. Cardinal has broader site development and utility work for residential, commercial and municipal clients.

agent_reason: Both are publicly listed active investment managers that sell fund products (mutual funds, ETFs) and separate accounts to institutional and individual investors. Both earn fees on assets managed. Cohen & Steers focuses on real assets and alternative income. Virtus runs a multi-boutique model that spans more strategies, including alternatives. The product type and the customers are the same.
notes_barbara:
Partial operating overlap. Different business mix

VRTS provides investment management products and services through affiliated boutique managers. CNS focuses on fee-based investment management centered on listed real assets.

agent_reason: Both are listed, fee-based investment managers that sponsor investment funds, including ETFs, for investors. Cohen & Steers is an active manager focused on real assets and alternative income. WisdomTree is a global asset manager that began with ETPs, and it now also holds a real-asset farmland manager (Ceres). Both serve investors and institutions, and both earn management fees on assets under management. The product mix differs: WisdomTree leans toward ETPs and digital assets, while Cohen & Steers leans toward active real-asset strategies. The overlap in fund products, investors and fee model is still enough for a direct peer.
notes_barbara:
Fund distribution overlap. Different investment focus

WisdomTree and Cohen & Steers manage funds for intermediaries and investors. WisdomTree primarily sponsors ETPs, while Cohen & Steers specializes in active listed real asset and preferred securities strategies.

agent_reason: Both are active, fee-based investment managers. Each runs pooled funds and separate accounts for institutional clients, intermediaries and individual investors. Cohen & Steers focuses on real assets and alternative income. Artisan covers active equity, fixed income and alternatives across autonomous teams. The product category (active investment management) and the customer base are the same. Only the strategy mix differs.
notes_barbara:
Partial operating overlap. Different business mix

APAM provides active investment management through autonomous investment teams running distinct equity, fixed income and alternative strategies. CNS focuses on fee-based investment management centered on listed real assets.

agent_reason: Cohen & Steers is an active investment manager of real assets and alternative income. It earns fees on assets under management from its own funds and separate accounts. Morningstar's website presents it as an investment research company offering fund, ETF and stock analysis, ratings, data and portfolio tools. Its revenue is mainly subscriptions, data and index licensing, and ratings fees. Morningstar does have a small managed-portfolio line, and both firms deal with advisors and institutions. But Morningstar mostly sells information and software to investors and asset managers, and Cohen & Steers mostly sells managed investment products.
notes_barbara:
Partial operating overlap. Different business mix

MORN provides independent investment research, ratings, data and analytics on funds, stocks and other securities to individual investors, financial advisors, asset managers and institutions. CNS focuses on fee-based investment management centered on listed real assets.

agent_reason: Both are diversified engineered-component manufacturers. Crane makes valves, pumps and flow-control equipment for chemical, energy and water customers. It also makes aerospace and defense components. ITT's Flow Technologies segment makes pumps and valves for energy, chemical and industrial customers, and its Aerospace Controls brand makes actuators and fluid control devices for aerospace and defense. Both sell products to OEMs and industrial users and add aftermarket sales. ITT also has automotive and rail friction and shock-absorber lines. Crane has no matching line, but the overlap covers both of Crane's material businesses.
notes_barbara:
Partial operating overlap. Different business mix

ITT designs and manufactures highly engineered critical components and flow-control equipment for transportation, industrial and energy customers. CR focuses on aerospace components and process flow equipment.

agent_reason: CRA sells economic, litigation and strategy consulting and expert testimony to law firms, corporations, accounting firms and governments. Jacobs sells engineering, design, project and construction management and infrastructure delivery to infrastructure owners, governments and industrial firms. The two share only the broad label "consulting" and some government and life-sciences clients. The services are different, and so are the core buyers (law firms versus infrastructure and facility owners).
notes_barbara:
Partial operating overlap. Different business mix

J provides consulting, engineering, design, project and program management, and construction management services. CRAI focuses on project-based economic, litigation and management consulting.

agent_reason: CorVel is a standalone outsourced claims, bill review and managed care provider. It sells to employers, insurers and TPAs, and its fees are per claim or per service. BBSI is a PEO and staffing firm. It co-employs client workers and handles payroll, HR, benefits and workers' comp coverage for small and mid-sized businesses. Its revenue comes from payroll-based PEO fees and staffing billings. BBSI's claims management and injury response is a minor add-on inside its risk services. Employers appear on both customer lists, but the core offering and the way each company earns money are different.
notes_barbara:
Workers’ compensation buyer overlap. Different service model

BBSI reaches employers through PEO and workforce services, including workers’ compensation support. CorVel sells claims and medical cost administration to employers and insurers.

agent_reason: Carlisle manufactures building envelope products (roofing membranes, insulation, waterproofing) sold through distributors and contractors. Comfort Systems USA is a mechanical/electrical/plumbing contractor that installs and services building systems on a project and service basis. Both serve commercial construction, but one makes and sells products and the other sells installation labor and services.
notes_barbara:
Building owner and contractor overlap. Different services

Comfort Systems installs and maintains mechanical and electrical systems. Carlisle sells commercial roofing, insulation and envelope products.

agent_reason: Both are building-envelope manufacturers selling roofing and insulation products through distributors and contractors, so there is real overlap. Carlisle is centered on commercial single-ply roofing, polyiso insulation and weatherproofing (CCM and CWT). Owens Corning's cited evidence points to a broader and more residential mix: shingles, insulation, doors and glass-fiber nonwovens and composites. Only the polyiso facer line (C:P2.7) is directly tied to commercial roofing, and it is a component sold into that market. Product and customer overlap are both partial, so this is adjacent, not a direct competitor.
notes_barbara:
Direct commercial insulation overlap. Different portfolio mix

Both sell commercial roof insulation to construction buyers. Owens Corning’s broader building materials portfolio and Carlisle’s membrane systems differ outside the shared product line.

agent_reason: Both are branded consumer apparel and footwear companies that design products and sell them through their own stores, e-commerce and wholesale retailers. The products differ. Deckers sells footwear (UGG, HOKA, Teva) with some related apparel. Carter's sells baby and children's apparel. The end consumers differ: Deckers sells to adult lifestyle and athletic buyers, while Carter's sells to parents buying for infants and children. The overlap is in the brand-owner/retail model and in some shared retail channels. That is not enough for a direct peer.
notes_barbara:
Different products and functional buyers

CRI designs, sources and markets apparel, sleepwear, bedding and accessories for babies and young children under its own brands. DECK focuses on branded performance and lifestyle footwear.

agent_reason: Dorman sells mechanical replacement parts (suspension, chassis, fasteners, brake lines) to auto parts retailers and distributors. XPEL sells paint protection film, window tint and coatings, mostly through installers and dealerships, and also runs its own installation shops. The products do not overlap: repair parts versus cosmetic and protective films. The main buyers differ too: parts retailers and warehouse distributors versus installers and dealers. The only link is that both are automotive aftermarket suppliers that use contract manufacturers.
notes_barbara:
Partial operating overlap. Different business mix

XPEL makes and sells paint protection film, window films, ceramic coatings and related products for vehicles, plus some architectural and marine uses. DORM focuses on replacement parts sold through automotive and heavy-duty aftermarket channels.

agent_reason: Both sell energy to residential and commercial customers. Con Edison is a regulated electric, gas and steam delivery utility in the New York City area. Suburban Propane is a nationwide, unregulated retail distributor of propane and other fuels, with some HVAC service. The customers overlap, but the products and the way they earn money differ. Con Edison earns regulated rates on delivery networks it owns. Suburban sells fuel by volume and charges for equipment service. That makes them adjacent, not direct.
notes_barbara:
Different core offering and revenue model

SPH distributes propane, fuel oil and refined fuels, natural gas and electricity to residential, commercial, industrial and agricultural customers. ED focuses on regulated delivery of electricity, gas and steam.

agent_reason: Both are regulated, asset-owning retail utilities that bill residential, commercial and government customers through a pipe or wire network at regulated rates. The commodities differ, though. Con Edison sells electricity, gas and steam. Artesian sells water and wastewater. Their service areas also differ. This is a neighboring utility overlap, not a direct competitor.
notes_barbara:
Different core offering and revenue model

ARTN.A provides drinking water and wastewater services to residential, commercial, industrial, and government customers, mainly in Delaware, with some service in Maryland and Pennsylvania. ED focuses on regulated delivery of electricity, gas and steam.

agent_reason: Both are rate-regulated utilities that own and operate delivery networks and bill residential and commercial customers directly. Con Edison sells electricity, gas and steam. Global Water sells water, wastewater and recycled water. The commodities differ, and the service areas are in different regions (New York versus Arizona). They share the regulated network-utility model and the kind of ratepayer, but not the product. That makes them adjacent, not direct.
notes_barbara:
Different core offering and revenue model

GWRS owns and operates regulated water, wastewater and recycled water utilities serving homes and businesses in master-planned communities in the Phoenix, Arizona area. ED focuses on regulated delivery of electricity, gas and steam.

agent_reason: Forestar develops residential land into finished homesites (lots) for builders, while NVR is a homebuilder that constructs and sells homes to homebuyers, with mortgage banking and title services. They share the residential housing end market, but NVR sits downstream of Forestar's product. NVR's buyers are homebuyers, not builders, and it earns money from home sales and mortgage banking rather than lot sales. They are therefore supplier and customer type, not competitors.
notes_barbara:
Residential development adjacency. Different buyers

NVR acquires lots and sells completed homes to consumers. Forestar develops lots for builders, placing the companies at different stages of residential development.

agent_reason: Ingles is mainly a grocery, pharmacy and fuel retailer. It earns money from product sales to household shoppers. SITE Centers is a pure open-air shopping center landlord. It earns rent from retail tenants. Ingles' real estate leasing is a minor side line, and the cited evidence shows it only as a grocery and pharmacy store operator. The two sell to different buyers: consumers versus retail tenants. Their business models and scale also differ.
notes_barbara:
Shopping center segment overlap. Different core economics

Ingles owns and leases some retail real estate, creating a segment overlap with SITE Centers. Grocery sales drive a different business model from collecting rent on a shopping center portfolio.

agent_reason: Ingles is a supermarket and pharmacy retailer selling groceries to household shoppers. Par Pacific is mainly a refiner. It produces fuels, buys crude and feedstocks, and sells the products it makes. Its customers are mostly wholesale, commercial, aviation and marine buyers. The only link is retail fuel sales to motorists, which is a small part of each business. The core businesses and the way each earns money are different.
notes_barbara:
Fuel retail segment overlap. Different core economics

Both sell fuel to motorists through retail locations. Ingles primarily operates supermarkets, while Par Pacific also refines and transports fuels.

agent_reason: Both are US multi-state, clinician-delivered healthcare service providers paid mainly by insurer and payor reimbursement. Both also partner with hospitals. The clinical offerings differ. Pediatrix provides physician specialty care in neonatal, maternal-fetal and pediatric medicine. USPh runs outpatient physical and occupational therapy clinics and an industrial injury prevention business. The patient populations differ (newborns, mothers and children versus orthopedic, sports and work-injury patients). The overlap is limited to the hospital relationship and the general healthcare-services model, so this is adjacent rather than a direct competitor.
notes_barbara:
Different products and functional buyers

USPH owns and operates outpatient physical and occupational therapy clinics treating patients with musculoskeletal injuries, post-surgical needs and work-related injuries. MD focuses on hospital-based neonatal, maternal and pediatric physician services.

agent_reason: NVR builds and sells finished homes to individual homebuyers, with mortgage and title services on top. Forestar develops raw land into finished lots and sells them to homebuilders, mainly its majority owner D.R. Horton. The two share only the residential housing end market. The products differ (homes vs. lots) and so do the customers (consumers vs. builders). Forestar is closer to a supplier to builders like NVR than a competitor.
notes_barbara:
Residential development adjacency. Different buyers

Forestar sells developed lots to homebuilders. NVR sells finished homes to consumers, so the link is through residential development and lot procurement.

agent_reason: Both are building-products manufacturers selling roofing and insulation through distributors and contractors. Owens Corning is centered on residential asphalt shingles, fiberglass insulation, and glass-fiber composites and nonwovens. Carlisle is centered on commercial single-ply roofing, polyiso insulation, and waterproofing, plus some aerospace and medical components. The product overlap is real but covers different roofing types and end-market focus, and Owens Corning's composites business has no Carlisle counterpart. That makes them adjacent rather than direct competitors.
notes_barbara:
Direct commercial insulation overlap. Different portfolio mix

Both sell insulation for commercial building envelopes. Carlisle emphasizes commercial roof systems, while Owens Corning serves a broader set of building materials markets.

agent_reason: OUTFRONT owns and operates billboard, transit and digital out-of-home displays and sells that ad space to brands and agencies. News Corp's evidence shows news and business information (Dow Jones), consumer book publishing (HarperCollins) and digital real estate services (Move/Realtor.com). It is a content and subscription publisher, not an out-of-home media owner. The two share only a loose link: both may sell advertising. The cited evidence does not show News Corp selling out-of-home or comparable ad space.
notes_barbara:
Partial operating overlap. Different business mix

NWSA publishes newspapers, digital news sites, and subscription news and professional information services, plus books and online real estate listing portals. OUT focuses on selling out-of-home billboard and transit advertising inventory.

agent_reason: Both are asset-based freight transport operators that sell freight services to B2B shippers for per-shipment or per-voyage fees. They differ in mode and customers. Pangaea runs ocean dry bulk shipping with ice-class vessels and port projects for commodity shippers. XPO runs North American less-than-truckload trucking for industrial and retail shippers. The shared asset-heavy freight model and some overlap among industrial shippers make them adjacent, but the product and the core customers are not the same.
notes_barbara:
Different products and functional buyers

XPO provides less-than-truckload (LTL) freight transportation for industrial, retail and commercial shippers in North America and Europe. PANL focuses on seaborne dry bulk shipping and related port logistics.

agent_reason: Par Pacific is mainly a refiner. Its evidence describes a refinery that buys crude and feedstocks and sells the refined products. Ingles is a supermarket and pharmacy chain that sells groceries to household shoppers. Retail fuel is a small side line for both companies, so there is no meaningful product or customer overlap.
notes_barbara:
Partial operating overlap. Different business mix

IMKT.A operates supermarkets in the southeastern US that sell groceries, fresh foods, pharmacy items, fuel and general merchandise to consumers. PARR focuses on refining, fuel logistics and branded retail fuel sales.

agent_reason: RMR is an external real estate manager and investment adviser. It sponsors and manages REITs, operating companies and private capital vehicles, and its customers are those managed entities. Orion is a self-managed single-tenant office REIT that owns buildings and earns rent from corporate and government tenants. The two share a commercial real estate end market. The business model and buyer differ, so Orion is not a useful comp for valuing RMR.
notes_barbara:
Commercial property exposure. Different revenue model

Orion owns and leases offices, while RMR earns management fees on real estate assets and vehicles. The property market overlap is narrower than the company-level business model.

agent_reason: RMR is a fee-earning investment and property manager that serves REITs, operating companies and private capital vehicles across all major real estate sectors. NHP is a REIT that owns healthcare properties and earns rent from healthcare operators and tenants. The only shared ground is commercial real estate, and NHP's senior housing and medical office focus touches only part of RMR's coverage. RMR sells management services to property owners and NHP sells leased space to tenants, so the products and the buyers differ.
notes_barbara:
Healthcare property exposure. Different revenue model

Healthcare real estate overlaps with part of RMR’s managed portfolio. The REIT earns rent from owned assets, while RMR earns fees for asset and operating management.

agent_reason: Both sell fiber broadband and phone service to residential and business subscribers over their own networks. But the comp is also a regulated electric utility, with hydro generation as a core business, and it serves remote Alaska. The target is a Mid-Atlantic fiber, video and wholesale carrier. The comp matches only the target's telecom side, so it gets at most 1.
notes_barbara:
Different end markets and offerings

APTL owns and operates electric generation (mostly hydro), transmission and distribution utilities serving remote communities in Alaska, plus local telephone, broadband and internet services. SHEN focuses on facilities-based regional fiber broadband for households and businesses.
